$comment: Release component pins: where every bundled sidecar and model comes from, and which bytes a release may ship. Read by scripts/build-component.sh (builds or fetches a component at its pin and installs it only if its sha256 matches) and checked by `node scripts/component-pins.mjs check` (CI, node job), which fails when this file, the build scripts, the bundle overlays, src-tauri/runtime-deps.sha256, release.yml and src-tauri/src/model.rs disagree.

Each artifact's digest lives in one place: its own sha256, or, for bytes uploaded to the runtime-deps prerelease, the pin of its runtime_deps_asset in src-tauri/runtime-deps.sha256 (release.yml verifies that pin before staging). Digests are of the bytes staged into src-tauri/binaries before bundling; Tauri then signs each externalBin with the Developer ID, so the copies inside a signed macOS app differ.

macOS cargo builds reproduce byte for byte only on the machine and build root that recorded them (the linker derives the Mach-O UUID from the output path; see scripts/build-component.sh). Linux pins are DGX-lane builds (v0.5.1 PROVENANCE-linux.txt for the components that did not move). A component whose rev moved lists its Linux targets under `pending`, with who builds them and how, until the DGX records them with build-component.sh --print-digest; nothing builds or stages a pending target (`component-pins.mjs pending` lists them). Since 2026-11-08 the aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu bytes are runtime_deps_asset pins that release.yml's release-linux-aarch64 job (ubuntu-24.04-arm) stages; with the DGX sold, a moved aarch64 pin is first built by that job's dry run (docs/RELEASE_LINUX.md).
federation: the citrate-federation manifest.toml pin of the source repo, and whether it matches. A mismatch is recorded with a note, never silent (Rule 11). Changing any pin is a reviewed PR.

Windows (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, from 0.5.9): every cargo sidecar links the C runtime statically (build.env CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_PC_WINDOWS_MSVC_RUSTFLAGS, which only a Windows target build reads), so a member's PC needs no Visual C++ Redistributable. The bytes are built on GitHub-hosted Windows runners by .github/workflows/release-windows.yml from the pinned revs; the run id that built each pin is in its evidence.

x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.why: 68434069 (#492) does not compile for Windows: core/storage/src/fd_limit.rs calls libc's rlimit API with no cfg(unix) (release-windows run 45451597501). This rev is 68434069 plus cfg-only commits in citrate-chain#494 that touch no consensus path (scripts/build-sidecar.sh refuses one that does). citrate-chain is squash-only, so this is the PR branch's commit itself, reachable through refs/pull/494 and the branch pin/windows-0.5.9-node (kept at this commit after the squash); 0.5.10 takes the squash on every OS. Owner OK 2026-11-24 (Windows onboarding).

x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.why: 755cf217 binds the bare basename pipe on Windows while this app connects to the per-install name (PBA-L7b-004), so Cluster IPC never connects there. This rev is 755cf217 plus the fix (citrate-cluster#19: endpoint_name derives citrate-core's per-install pipe name; Unix unchanged; Windows CI job). citrate-cluster is squash-only with linear history and main has moved past 755cf217 (V60 mesh), so this is #19's fix commit itself, reachable through refs/pull/19 and the branch pin/windows-0.5.9-cluster-daemon (created to keep it; #19 was squash-merged to main as f720e105 for 0.5.10). macOS and Linux keep 755cf217 for 0.5.9.
